reason: A keeps the original centred stack and hierarchy (logo, can, headline, CTA, legal), but the can is undersized, there is a dead gap between can and headline, and the legal line is tiny at the bottom. B blows the can up until it dominates, pushes the headline down against the bottom-left edge, shrinks the CTA to a small pill crammed into the bottom-right corner, and squeezes the legal into an unreadable four-line block under it, so the CTA is buried and the layout feels lopsided.

Both have the same breakage. The cream circle that sat behind the can has come loose and is cut off in the bottom-left corner. Without it the orange can disappears into the orange background, leaving only a 'SOLSTICE' band and two green dots. The headline is small and left-aligned while the can and buttons are centred, and the NEW pill and Try It button float in empty space. A is worse because the faint can sits at the top and the headline at mid-height, so it reads product first, then message. B at least follows brand/headline → product → NEW → CTA, with a slightly larger product. B still has a big empty gap between the subcopy and the can.

A: the cream circle has come apart from the product and sits clipped in the bottom-left corner. The can's body is now the same orange as the background, so the product reads as an empty outline. The NEW badge floats alone in the top-right corner. Still, the right column (headline, then subcopy, then CTA) keeps a sensible order and alignment, even if it is loosely spaced. B: the product has shrunk to an unreadable thumbnail jammed against the left edge, and the cream circle sits clipped in the corner. The subcopy has fallen far below the headline, with the NEW badge and CTA strung across the middle between them, so the reading order is broken. The layout is mostly dead space.

A separates the cream circle from the bottle and drops it into the bottom-left corner, cut off by the edge. That leaves an orange-on-orange bottle with almost no contrast, a small headline floating in a mostly empty canvas, left-aligned text next to a centred CTA, and a large gap above 'Out now.'. B keeps the bottle-on-circle motif intact and at a good scale, but 'Out now.' is cut off from the headline and sits alone at the bottom right across from the CTA, the headline is jammed against the top of the circle, and the bottom row feels cramped.

A keeps the original's structure: the quote mark sits top-left, then the quote, then the attribution in a left column, with the can and circle on the right. It needs fixes before shipping. 'too soon.' is left alone on the last line. The SOLSTICE logo is centred under the column instead of sitting on the text's left edge, and it is larger than in the original. B wraps the quote into 5 cramped lines that start almost at the top edge. Its quote mark hangs at mid-height beside the text, which looks arbitrary. The attribution is enlarged until it competes with the quote, and the logo again floats off-axis.

A keeps the quote as the clear focal point: it is large and well wrapped, with the gold quote mark tucked beside it and the attribution directly below. The product and circle sit bottom-right as in the original. Its flaws are minor: the logo floats in a gap on the left and the SOLSTICE label is unreadably tiny. B gets the hierarchy wrong: the oversized quote mark dominates while the quote shrinks to small text crammed into the top-right. The logo is jammed directly under the attribution, and the product is centred at the bottom, cut off from the text.

Both share the same serious flaws. The SAVE 15% badge is blown up into the largest element and runs off the left canvas edge, so it overpowers the headline. The coffee bag, the key product image, has shrunk to an unreadable icon jammed between the CTA and a tiny logo. The right side is a blurry, empty photo block with nothing on it. A is worse because its body copy wraps onto two cramped lines and crowds the CTA, while B keeps the body copy on one line under a slightly larger headline, which gives a cleaner left-to-right read, although B leaves more dead dark space at the far right.

A breaks the hero image: the shoe has come off its lime circle, which now hangs half-hidden in the bottom-right like a separate shape. The logo sits oddly after the NEW VIDEO badge on one row, the headline is small and wraps 'marathons' onto its own line, and the bottom-left is empty. B keeps the original's structure: logo top-left, badge top-right and a large, dominant two-line headline. Its flaws are a shoe that is too big and spills past its circle, a shoe group shifted left that leaves the right side empty, and 'Full review inside.' pushed apart from the headline down to the bottom edge.

A: the 'INKWELL & LANTERN' logo sits against the left canvas edge, which hurts the brand mark. The '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' kicker is shrunk to a tiny red fragment at the bottom left, cut off from the headline. The headline is squeezed into three lines in a narrow right column, so the layout reads as two disconnected halves. B: the hierarchy is clear (kicker, then a large two-line headline, then body copy, then the CTA) and the logo is intact top right. Its flaws: the terrazzo background is almost gone, the book art is shrunk to a small corner thumbnail, the body copy is nearly as heavy as the CTA and crowds the left edge, and the legal line under the button is tiny.

A: the three plan cards are drawn at very different sizes. Family is huge and the Yearly and Monthly cards are tiny, so their labels can't be read and the original hierarchy, where the dark Yearly card was the hero, is flipped. The cards are scattered left and right around a ragged, left-aligned subtitle. B: the cards are a consistent size but far too small, so their labels can't be read. They are out of order (Yearly and Family on top, Monthly stranded alone below the subtitle), and the subtitle sits between the cards; the logo has also moved to the right edge. B wins narrowly, only because its cards are at least the same scale.

A is just the original block shrunk and centred. It takes up about a third of the banner and leaves huge dead areas on both sides, so it is not a rearrangement for the wide format, and the fine print is tiny. B does rearrange the design left to right: phone, then a one-line headline, then the CTA. But the phone is jammed almost against the top and bottom edges, the CTA sits isolated far to the right across a large empty gap, the CTA is undersized, and the '7 days free' line is illegibly small.

A keeps the logo top-left, the badge top-right and a big two-line headline with a clear order. But the shoe is now larger than its green circle and sits off-centre over it, losing the original's framed-disc look. 'Full review inside.' is also jammed under the sole with little bottom margin. B's layout is broken. The NEW VIDEO badge and logo share one row in swapped, arbitrary positions. The headline shrank and wraps awkwardly ('...on 100 / marathons'). The green circle has come apart from the shoe and drifts to the bottom-right, leaving a lopsided composition with dead space on the left.

A: the terrazzo confetti background is gone entirely, which strips the brand feel and leaves a flat beige panel. The book cover shrinks to a tiny top-left thumbnail, the body copy is nearly as heavy as the CTA, and the footer legal line is cramped against the bottom edge. B: the confetti and cover art survive in a deliberate two-column layout with a clear headline, body and CTA stack on the right. But the '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' eyebrow is shrunk to illegible micro-text under the logo, and the 'INKWELL & LANTERN' wordmark is oversized and competes with the book.

A keeps the original's centred top-to-bottom order and a strong CTA. But the headline leaves the word 'last' alone on its own line, and the legal line is moved above the CTA at almost subhead size, crowding the subhead-legal-button stack while the top half has empty space. B breaks the hierarchy: the CTA shrinks to a small pill buried in a narrow right column, the body copy wraps awkwardly ('sunrise to / sunset on / June 21.'), the legal text is nearly as big as the CTA, and the small bottle floats at left beside a large dead centre. The huge headline also crowds the bottom-left corner.

A separates the green circle from the can and leaves it as a stray blob in the bottom-left. The CTA has shrunk into a tiny pill jammed against the badges, which wrap onto a second row. Body copy is too small to read, the brand mark sits under the headline, and a large dead zone is left at the top. B keeps the can centered in its circle, with the brand then the headline as in the original, so it reads as the same design. Its flaws: the headline is set off-center to the right, the CTA is shrunk to the same size as the badges so it no longer stands out, and the three pills fill the bottom row edge to edge with little margin.

A keeps the product on its circle, but the can sticks out past the top of the circle and nearly touches the canvas top. GLACIER now sits below the headline, so the brand is out of order and as big as a second headline. The CTA has shrunk to a chip the same size as the two badges, and the copy and button row are crammed against the bottom edge. B breaks the design: the teal circle is left as an empty disc on the left and the can is cut off from it and pushed to the far right, so the main image is split into two meaningless pieces. B also keeps every flaw of A: GLACIER below the headline and a tiny CTA that is no more prominent than the badges.

A squeezes the whole text block into the top-right corner and leaves the left half and bottom third as dead orange space. Its headline is shrunk until it barely outweighs the italic subline, so the original's centred, confident hierarchy is lost. B keeps a large centred headline that dominates as it should, but its bottom row is cramped: the left-aligned subline 'Now in four flavours.' and the CTA sit tight against the bottom and right edges. That row breaks the centred axis, and the 'a little / sunshine.' wrap is clumsy, so it needs polish but reads far better.

A rescales the headline well for the tall format and keeps a strong hierarchy. It has clear flaws, though: a large dead gap separates the headline from the bottom row, the subline wraps awkwardly ('Now in four / flavours.') and is squeezed beside the CTA, and that left-right pair breaks the centred axis of the original. B is just a shrunk copy of the original. Its headline is small for the canvas, the subline and CTA label are nearly illegibly tiny, and the three elements float far apart with big empty bands between them, so the layout loses its grouping and its intent.

A is only a uniform shrink. It keeps the original grouping and hierarchy, but the 'LIMITED' badge is now tiny and close to illegible, the CTA text is small, and the block sits in a wide band of dead orange space with no use of the wider format. B fills the banner with an oversized headline that almost touches the left and right edges and crowds the top. Its CTA shrinks to a minor element, and the 'LIMITED' badge is pulled away from the button and stranded on the right, so the badge/CTA grouping is broken and the bottom row looks arbitrary.

A keeps the right order (headline, then CTA) on a centred axis, but the LIMITED badge has drifted to the bottom-left corner, far from the button it belongs with. A large dead gap sits between the CTA and the badge, the CTA is undersized, and 'Bubbles,' is left alone on its own line. B is worse: it pushes the CTA and badge into the top-left corner, jammed against the canvas edge and above the headline, so the reading order is inverted. The headline floats low with empty space above, and it also breaks into four ragged lines.

A breaks up the copy block. 'Every mixed case.' floats at top centre, away from its '20% off' headline. The CTA sits in the top-right corner, the legal line hangs alone at mid-right, and the headline is jammed into a circle cropped by the bottom edge. Reading order is jumbled. B keeps the original grouping intact (eyebrow, headline, subline, CTA, then product on its circle), but the whole cluster is pushed into the middle. That leaves a ~220px dead band on the left and empty space on the right, the legal line is stranded far below, and it reads as the square layout dropped onto a banner rather than one designed for it.

A is broken: the bottle has come off its cream circle, which now sits empty at the bottom-left and gets cut off at the edge. The bottle is tiny, everything is squeezed into a thin middle strip with large dead areas above and below, and the stray faint circle at the top-left reads as an accident. B puts the bottle back on its circle at a good size and keeps the headline, NEW badge and Try It button clearly readable. Its flaws: the bottle cap sticks out past the circle, the headline floats centred while the row below starts at the left, there is a lot of empty orange on the right, and the stray faint circle at the top-left is still there.

A is just the square layout shrunk and centred: wide dead bands left and right, a tiny unreadable attribution and logo, and the circle drifting into the area beside the quote, so it doesn't suit the banner format. B rearranges into a proper two-column banner with large readable quote text and the can and circle as a strong right-hand focal point; its flaws are a big gap between the quote mark and the quote, the text block sitting close to the bottom edge, and the logo moved inside the circle under the can.

A: the headline is oversized and jammed against the left edge. The logo has shrunk to a tiny dot inside the circle. The steps break the reading order: 01 and 02 share the top row while 03 drops below, so the grid is ragged. The step text is tiny, and step 01's text is set noticeably smaller than step 02's. The legal line is illegible. B is much worse: the steps are out of order (02 and 03 on top, 01 below), and 01 is shrunk to unreadable microtext. An enormous CTA pill overpowers the headline. The logo, the 'Pour-over, properly' kicker and the legal line are crammed into illegible specks at the far right edge.

A blows the '24 HOURS, 24 READERS' eyebrow up into a huge two-line orange block with an awkward '24 / READERS' break, so it competes with the headline and the body copy. Both candidates jam the Inkwell & Lantern logo into the far-left confetti strip, where it sits on a busy background and its 'LANTERN' text runs across the card edge. Both also have tiny, ragged fine print under the CTA. B keeps the eyebrow small and subordinate, so its hierarchy is cleaner, but the logo problem still needs fixing before it could ship.

A reads left to right as a banner should (product bag, then headline, then CTA), but the CITRINE logo has been dropped. The bag is shrunk to a smudge where the QUILLBROOK label can't be read, and the 'Find a Store' button text is tiny. B keeps the CITRINE wordmark, but the product bag is lost or turned into a dark block. Its CTA is a microscopic pill wedged under the logo, colliding with that block and placed before the headline, so the reading order is backwards and the CTA is buried.

A: the orange divider line cuts straight through 'Rosemary' in the headline, which is a visible collision. The dark brand header bar is gone, the 'Reserve a Case' button is shrunk to a tiny pill in the bottom-left that no longer stands out, and the oversized logo competes with the headline. Even so, it reads in a sensible order (headline, body, CTA, legal). B: a leftover strip of the dark header sits cut off at the top-right and looks like an accident. The body copy is squeezed into a narrow right column with choppy one- and two-word lines, and the CTA, 'Ships late June' and legal text are crammed under it. The headline sits stranded bottom-left, so the halves split awkwardly and the reading order is jumbled. Both are broken, but B is worse.

A: the bottom is cramped into a three-column row. The subcopy is squeezed into a narrow 4-line column, and the legal text is a tiny, ragged 7-line column jammed beside the CTA. The bottle floats off-axis on the left with dead space to its right, and the logo and ribbon sit at unrelated heights. B: keeps a clear centered top-to-bottom reading order with a strong CTA. But the headline orphans 'last' on its own line, the legal text is promoted above the CTA almost as large as the subcopy (and orphans 'Co., 2026.'), and the logo floats at an arbitrary right-of-center spot instead of sharing an edge with the ribbon.

A puts the CTA first at the far left, jammed against the canvas edge, so the reading order runs backwards. Its legal text is set as large as the subhead and competes with it, and the 'Longest Day Sale' ribbon is shrunk to an illegible sticker crammed against the end of the subhead. B reads correctly from logo to product to headline to CTA and keeps the legal text subordinate. Its flaws: the CTA is crammed against the right edge and nearly touches the end of the subhead ('June 21.'), the sale ribbon is tiny and squeezed under the legal line, and there is a dead gap between the bottle and the headline.

A: the body copy sits first at the far left, ahead of the headline and on top of a leftover piece of the circle, so the reading order is jumbled. The headline is small and the badges are stacked loosely on the right. Its CTA is still a clear, legible button. B: the two-line headline dominates well, but the CTA has shrunk to a tiny pill crammed top-right. The badges are jammed against it and the body copy is microscopic and illegible, so the action is buried in an overstuffed right cluster.

A keeps a sensible top-to-bottom order (brand, headline, large product), but the CTA 'Find It Near You' has shrunk to a tiny pill the same size as the badges, which buries the action. The body copy is pushed to the bottom below the buttons, so the reading order is reversed, and there are large dead gaps above and below the button row. B is scattered on two columns with no clear logic: the product is shrunk into the top-right corner, the headline floats on the left with no link to the content beside it, the CTA and badges float far apart in the right column, the body copy wraps in a narrow column at the bottom right, and the big empty areas leave the layout looking unintentional.

A is basically a shrunk copy of the original with wide empty side margins and no real rearrangement for the wider shape. The subhead and badge text are now very small, but hierarchy, grouping and brand stay intact. B rearranges the layout but breaks it: the phone hero image is cut down to a tiny icon jammed against the left edge, with its circle clipped. The subhead is set larger than the CTA label. The CTA sits in a row of three same-size pills, so the badges compete with it equally, and the SOLSTICE wordmark is a tiny fragment beside a huge headline.

A keeps the original's type sizes and spreads the three elements down the square. That leaves huge, uneven gaps: the subline floats far from the headline it supports, the CTA is cut off from both, and the headline is undersized for the canvas, so it reads as stretched spacing, not a redesign. B gives the headline a bold 4-line size and a strong focal point that suits the square. But its bottom row is awkward: the centre-aligned 3-line subline sits jammed under the headline and doesn't line up with the right-shifted CTA, which breaks the central axis and crowds the bottom margin.

A keeps the original's reading order (eyebrow, headline, subhead, CTA, then product) on a clean left edge with a big shoe. Its flaws: the peach circle has shrunk into a cut-off blob in the bottom-right corner that no longer frames the shoe, the legal line is tiny, and the lower half feels loose. B breaks the hierarchy because the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow drops below the subhead, so it reads as orphaned copy. B's circle also sits behind the headline instead of the product, a dead gap separates the shoe from the CTA pushed to the bottom, and its legal text is just as tiny.

A: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' kicker has shrunk to tiny type crammed beside the headline, the body copy is squeezed into a narrow column with one or two words per line ('Every / mixed / case of'), the bottle is oversized and overpowers the 20% headline, and the peach circle has slid into the bottom corner where it crowds the CTA and gets cropped. B: it has a clean top-to-bottom stack with a dominant headline and a centred bottle and CTA, but 'WEEKEND ONLY' has moved below the body copy, which breaks the original reading order. The body copy wraps to leave an orphaned 'sparkling.', the left-aligned text block and the centred bottle and button sit on two different axes, and there is dead space at the bottom.

A: the product roundel has shrunk to a tiny circle crammed against the top edge, and the bottle is cropped to a dark stub, so the key product image is effectively gone and reads as a glitch; the NEW badge and Try It button stack neatly on the right. B: the bottle is kept and recognisable, but its circle runs into the 't' of 'Sunset' (an unwanted collision), the NEW badge overlaps the top of Try It and is clipped by the canvas edge, and the button crowds the right edge. B is slightly less bad because it keeps the product.

A: the headline 'Blood Orange Sunset' runs into the phone and its cream circle, which is a clear collision. The subline is split off from its headline and sits under the CTA on the far right, so the reading order is jumbled and the copy grouping is broken. B: it keeps the original's left-to-right order and grouping, but it has real flaws. The cream circle has slipped below the phone and is cropped at the bottom edge, and the phone is tiny. There is a large dead gap between the headline and the subline, and the 'Online only' badge floats awkwardly away from the CTA.

A keeps the original's centred order intact (logo, kicker, headline, subtitle, date, chips, RSVP), but it is basically a narrowed copy rather than a re-layout: the chip labels are tiny, there is a large dead band between the chips and the RSVP and another empty zone at the bottom, and the can floats off the grid at the right. B breaks the reading order: 'SOLSTICE PRESENTS' is cut off from the headline and parked at the left, the subtitle sits in a cramped left column beside the date, the RSVP CTA comes above the info chips, and the chips are stacked vertically with uneven gaps, so the details read as scattered fragments. B also leaves the oversized can and the placeholder box fighting for weight with no clear grid.

A is the original layout dropped into the taller canvas without rearranging it: every element stays at its original small size in a band across the middle, with large dead areas above and below, so it reads as a letterboxed copy. B actually rearranges the design and gives it a strong headline and a large shoe and CTA, but it has flaws: the copy wraps awkwardly ('closes / Thursday.'), the oversized LIMITED pill sits beside the CTA and competes with it instead of staying subordinate, and the headline (left edge ~28px) and copy column (~357px) don't share an alignment axis.

A just spreads the banner's elements down the taller canvas: the shoe stays small, there are big empty bands at the top and bottom, and the headline, copy and LIMITED pill sit far apart in a loose column, so it looks like a stretched banner rather than a new layout. B rebuilds the layout with a large shoe as the hero and the headline at top left, but the copy and CTA float on the right away from the headline, 'Thursday.' is left alone on its own line, the Enter Now button has shrunk and the LIMITED pill beside it competes with it, and the shoe looks slightly stretched sideways.

Both candidates have the same broken structure. The three equal price cards end up at three different sizes and heights (Monthly smallest and lowest, Family largest), which breaks the side-by-side comparison and makes Family stand out over the highlighted Yearly plan. The subhead is a cramped centred block jammed above Monthly, and the legal text is unreadably small under the CTA. A is marginally better because it leaves slightly more room at the edges. B pushes the Monthly card (about 26px) and the CTA closer to the canvas edges and is otherwise nearly identical.

A just drops the original square layout into the middle of the banner: the headline and phone sit in a narrow centre column with about 220px of dead space on each side, so it reads as a pasted-in square, not a banner. B is actually rearranged left to right (headline, phone, CTA), and the headline wrapping onto two lines suits the width. But B's CTA sits higher than the headline's centre line, the phone separates the CTA from its headline, and the price line floats far below the CTA instead of sitting with it.

A keeps a clean centred stack, but the headline wraps to leave 'last' orphaned on its own line, the legal line is moved above the CTA where it crowds the subcopy and competes with it, and the CTA is oversized, leaving the lower band cramped. B breaks the grid: the bottle sits off-axis on the left above a large dead gap, the offer copy is squeezed into a narrow ragged column beside the CTA, and the fine print is crammed into a tiny, barely legible column on the right edge, so the bottom row reads as scattered fragments.

A is scattered across a broken two-column grid. The product circle is tiny and floats top-right. The CTA has shrunk to a minuscule pill sitting level with the badges, and FREE DELIVERY and SUMMER ONLY float in dead space. The body copy is stranded at the bottom right, below the badges, so reading order collapses and there is a lot of empty space. B keeps a sensible top-to-bottom order: brand, headline, product, actions. But the CTA is squeezed to the same small size as the three badges in one row, so it is buried, the body copy is left alone at the bottom after the CTA, and large empty bands sit around the button row.

A breaks the reading order: the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow drops below the subhead and reads as an afterthought. The headline is jammed into the peach circle, the top band is dead space, the gap between the sneaker and the CTA is too large, and the legal line is microscopic. B keeps the original eyebrow, headline, subhead and CTA stack on a clean left edge with good hierarchy. Its flaws: the circle is pulled away from the sneaker and parked as a cropped blob in the bottom-right corner, nearly touching the legal line; the centred sneaker doesn't line up with the left-aligned text column; there's a dead gap below the CTA; and the legal text is too small.

A keeps the bottle visible with its label, but the bottle sits jammed against the end of 'Sunset' with no gutter, and the NEW pill is stacked on top of the Try It button so the two overlap. B has the same overlap between NEW and the button, and it also shrinks the bottle into a tiny circle cropped off the top edge, so the product image, a key brand element, is effectively lost.

A keeps the original left-to-right order, but the phone has slid off its cream circle and the circle is cut off at the bottom edge. There is also a large dead gap between the headline and the tagline, so the type block looks loose and the phone group looks broken. B is worse: the headline runs into the phone and circle, which split it from its tagline, and the tagline now sits stranded under the CTA on the right. That jumbles the reading order and destroys the headline–subcopy grouping.

Both cut the dark header into an empty block at the top right, which leaves the white SOLSTICE wordmark on cream where it can't be read, so the brand breaks in both. A: the headline is big and fills the banner well. But the bottom row is jammed against the bottom edge: body copy, CTA, an oversized 'Ships late June' that competes with the CTA, and legal text too small to read. The orange divider is stranded under the logo. B is a shrunk, centred copy of the portrait original: the headline is small, the body, CTA label and legal text are tiny, the divider floats off to the right at random, and there is a lot of dead space on both sides.

A keeps a clean centred axis and the original order, but the dark header band floats with an odd cream strip above it. The orange rule has moved from under the headline to under the eyebrow, and there are big dead gaps between the headline, the body copy and the CTA. B also floats the header band, and it moves the eyebrow into the band, which changes the brand header. Its headline is centred while the body copy and the 'Reserve a Case' button shift left onto a different axis, so the left edge is ragged and nothing reads as aligned. It has the same large empty gaps, and its legal text is microscopic.

A breaks the product apart: the sage circle sits alone at the far left while the can is pushed to the far right, so you get two leftover fragments with empty space on both sides of the text. The body copy is also unreadably small and the SOLSTICE wordmark now sits under the headline. B makes the same text mistakes: the wordmark is under the headline, the body copy is tiny, and the CTA is crammed in among the badges. B's circle is also cut off at the left edge and the can sits beside it rather than on it. But B keeps the product on the left and the copy on the right, so it reads left to right like a banner and is the less broken of the two.

A: the 'Find It Near You' CTA shrinks to a tiny pill crammed into the top-right corner next to the two badges, which gives it the same weight as they have. The rotated 'Free Delivery' badge collides with the shrunken product, and the body copy is illegibly small. B: the CTA is at least a clear dark button under the headline, but GROVE drops below the headline, the 'Summer Only' and 'Free Delivery' badges are piled on the left edge with no product next to them, and the body text on the right is unreadably small. B is less bad because its CTA hierarchy and left-to-right flow still work.

A: the green circle is cut off from the phone and left as a blank blob on the left. The tagline is stranded at the far right after the phone, so the reading order breaks. The CTA and the two pills sit jammed together in one row, which puts the button on the same level as the badges. B has the same circle-and-phone split and the same crowded CTA row, and it is worse: the tagline sits on top of the circle and is pressed against the left edge of the canvas, so the ad opens with small secondary copy and the hierarchy is wrong.

A is just the original shrunk and centred: the subhead is so small it's unreadable and the CTA label is tiny, while wide empty bands sit on both sides, so it doesn't use the banner shape at all. B does rearrange for the banner, with a big, legible headline on the left and the copy and CTA in a right-hand column. But the subhead is squeezed into a narrow five-line column with ragged breaks, and it sits almost against the top edge. The CTA is crammed near the bottom-right corner with little margin, and the right column is cramped next to the roomy headline.

A is just a shrunk, centered copy of the original. The 'Now in four flavours' line and the CTA label are tiny and barely legible at banner size, and wide empty orange bands sit on both sides, so it does not suit the banner shape. B does rearrange the design into a banner (headline on the left, subline and CTA in a right column), but it is cramped: the headline nearly touches the left and top edges, its full stop almost hits the CTA, the CTA is undersized, and the subline breaks awkwardly as 'Now in four / flavours.'

Both put the SOLSTICE wordmark below the headline, reverse the flavour pill order, and shrink the subhead to unreadable fine print. A is worse: everything is jammed against the right side, with the headline nearly touching the Shop Flavours button, the subhead wrapped into three illegible lines, and a large dead area on the left. B moves the group left, leaves a cleaner gap before the CTA and wraps the subhead in two lines, but its subhead is still too small and the left side is still mostly empty.

A keeps a logical left-to-right flow (headline → copy → CTA), but the product can shrinks to an unreadable orange sliver, the 'WEEKEND ONLY' eyebrow is cut off from the headline and parked over the legal text at the far right, and the legal text is tiny and cramped. B keeps the can and the peach circle better, but it puts the CTA first: 'Shop Sale' is jammed against the left canvas edge ahead of the headline, the eyebrow is separated from '20% off', and the legal text is squeezed into a tiny, crowded block at the right edge. B's reading order is broken in the more serious way.
